title: Customer action lanes for partial-degradation and replay choices
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, customer-facing communications draft that can be reused for partial-degradation incidents where some requests returned truncated or partially structured outputs (examples: structured JSON truncation, streaming session drop, a subset of regions seeing premature EOS). The goal is to (1) provide a short status update suitable for a status page; (2) provide a concise post-incident customer summary; and (3) offer clear, mutually exclusive customer action lanes (choices) for replay/verification/opt-out, with the evidence items we will provide for each lane.

Audience
- Primary: affected customers (engineering/product leads, platform teams)
- Secondary: internal CS/SEs preparing bespoke outreach

Quick TL;DR (status page snippet)
- Title: Partial degradation affecting structured output and streaming in EU and US-west (intermittent)
- Impact: Some API requests returned truncated or partially-structured responses between 2026-06-21 17:32 UTC and 2026-06-21 18:30 UTC. Affected tenants may observe missing keys or early EOS tokens for a fraction of requests.
- Current status: Remediated; routing and model fallback policies reverted. Follow-up: offering optional replay and validation evidence to tenants.
- Link: status.redwood.com/incidents/PRTL-2026-06-21

Concise customer-facing post-incident summary (one pager)
- What happened: During a ~58-minute window our routing layer and model variant fallback policy misaligned when a kernel upgrade rolled out to a subset of pods. That misalignment caused an edge case in the KV-cache handling which occasionally dropped the final structured tokens (truncation) or produced premature stream termination. Only requests that hit the affected pod pool and used structured-output mode were at risk.
- Scope: Estimated ~0.7% of production generation requests across EU and US-west. No embeddings or metadata stores were impacted. No customer data exfiltration.
- Root cause (top-line): kernel rollout (internal runtime release) + routing policy race => intermittent KV-cache staleness => truncated output on some responses. Full RCA will be posted to Confluence and linked on the incident page.
- What we did: Immediate rollback of the rollout from the impacted pool, force-evicted affected pods, ran targeted validation prompt tests, revalidated model outputs against canonical prompt set, and reenabled conservative fallback policies.
- Customer-facing remediation and safeguards: We’ve added an extra validation gate to rollout orchestration (block on KV-cache version check) and added a temporary rule to prefer fully-validated pods for structured-output routes during rollouts.

Customer action lanes (choose one):
We want customers to be able to select how they want us to handle potentially affected requests. Each lane is mutually exclusive; choosing one lets us provide an evidence package tailored to that workflow. Include the chosen lane in a reply to your account owner or the incident contact.

1) Automatic replay + evidence (recommended for most production apps)
- What we do: We will automatically replay candidate requests that match the same tenant, model, and prompt hash against the validated pool and supply new responses. We will annotate responses with a replay_id and provide a short reconciliation report that shows original vs replayed outputs and confidence tags (match / partial / different).
- Evidence provided: replay_id list, timestamps, original response snippet (truncated portion highlighted), replayed response(s), boolean match flag, per-response token counts, and reproducibility score.
- Timeline: Start replay within 48 hours of receiving your opt-in; aim to complete within 72 hours.
- Caveats: Replayed responses may differ (model nondeterminism); we surface both variants. Replays are best-effort for requests where we have a matching prompt and tenant association.

2) Manual verification package (for conservative/regulatory workflows)
- What we do: We prepare an evidence kit you can use to run your own verification: sanitized request logs, original response artifacts, canonical prompt definitions, failure rate summary, and a small sample of raw token streams. We will not perform replays unless explicitly requested afterwards.
- Evidence provided: sanitized logs (timestamps + request hashes), sample originals (redacted to protect other tenants), guidance for verification tests, and recommended acceptance checks.
- Timeline: Kit available within 72 hours of request.

3) Opt-out (no replay, no data retained beyond standard retention)
- What we do: No action taken. We will not replay requests or send additional artifacts beyond the incident summary.
- Evidence provided: brief confirmation that opt-out was received and the incident summary.
- Timeline: immediate; no further action unless you later request a different lane.

4) Service credit + tailored remediation plan (commercial route)
- What we do: Work with your customer success and account teams to evaluate quantitative impact and propose a proportional service credit or commercial concession. Also available: on-call engineering review and bespoke engineering remediation work for your integrations (e.g., pre-rollout guard rails).
- Evidence provided: hit-rate and error-rate analysis, request-level sample set, proposed credit calculation.
- Timeline: propose within 7 business days after lane selection.

How to choose and how to ask
- Reply to this email to your account owner with: chosen_lane: <one of [automatic_replay, manual_verification, opt_out, credit_and_remediation]>, primary_contact: <name + email>, and any constraints (e.g., only replays for prompts X,Y).
- If we don’t hear back within 10 business days we will default to Opt-out.

Evidence and privacy notes
- We will never share raw requests that contain PII or secrets. If a suspected request contains customer secrets we will redact according to our data-handling policy and coordinate with your security contact.
- Replay only uses stored prompt/tenant associations and does not pull sensitive external resources. Replayed responses are produced by the same model family; we will include a note on nondeterminism.

Short FAQ (for status page or support threads)
- Q: Will you replay everything?
  A: No — only requests where we can reliably match the original prompt hash and tenant and where the output appears truncated/different. We also respect opt-out.
- Q: Will replays change my billing?
  A: No. Replays for remediation are provided at no charge for affected requests.
- Q: Can replays introduce different outputs?
  A: Yes. Replays are probabilistic; we supply both variants with confidence/reproducibility metadata so you can decide which to accept.

Next steps (internal checklist for CS)
- Prepare per-tenant list of candidate request hashes (data team).
- Account teams confirm lane selection and primary contact.
- Engineering run replays (if chosen) and compile reconciliation report.
- Deliver evidence kit or confirmation to customer, log selection and timeline in JIRA-OPS-8891.

Contact
- Primary incident contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- Escalation (engineering): Marco Chen, eng-incident@redwood.com

Notes and open questions (internal)
- Need legal signoff for replaying requests that may include developer-provided PII; queued with privacy team (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Confirm whether we ship full token streams in evidence kit or truncated to last 256 tokens (privacy vs utility tradeoff).
- Add a status-page short form that maps lane names to short action buttons for self-serve selection in future incidents.

-- end of draft --

Author notes
- This is intentionally concise (one-pager + structured choice lanes) so CS can paste the status snippet and the one-pager into a customer thread and attach the lane selection mechanism. Keep as a living template.
